subject: def-fd-periodic-fourier-sobolev-spaces

before.quote: **Trigonometric polynomials.** A **trigonometric polynomial** on $\mathbb T$ is a finite complex linear combination of characters, $p=\sum_{k\in F}c_ke_k$, for a finite $F\subseteq\mathbb Z$ and scalars $c_k\in\mathbb C$. The set of all trigonometric polynomials is the span of $\{e_k:k\in\mathbb Z\}$; it is closed under addition, scalar multiplication, multiplication and complex conjugation (by the identities for $e_ke_l$ and $\overline{e_k}$), and it contains $e_0=1$. Nothing is claimed here about uniqueness of the coefficients in an expansion, nor about the size of $\widehat p$; those are properties of the characters proved below.

after.quote:
**The finite torus.** On $\mathbb T^n$, $n\ge1$, the characters are
$e_k(x):=\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot x)$ for $k\in\mathbb Z^n$, where $k\cdot x$ is the
Euclidean dot product of a representative tuple; trigonometric polynomials are
finite complex linear combinations of these, and Fourier coefficients of
$f\in L^1(\mathbb T^n;\mathbb C)$ are
$\widehat f(k)=\int_{\mathbb T^n}f\,e_{-k}\,dm_{\mathbb T^n}$. Fubini computes
integrals of products of characters on the product measure
([[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]); for
$f\in L^2(\mathbb T^n;\mathbb C)$ Hölder's inequality makes $f\,e_{-k}$
integrable ([[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]],
[[thm-finite-measure-l-r-includes-into-l-p-for-p-less-r]]).

before.claim: Symmetric truncations to $|k|_\infty\le M$ converge in the weighted \ell^2 norm by convergence of the defining nonnegative series. Conjugate symmetry is preserved, so the completion is the real weighted coefficient subspace. For $s\ge0$, $w_k^{2s}\ge1$, so [F4] gives the unique $L^2$ representative; for $s<0$ the construction gives only the coefficient completion.

after.claim:
Since $w_k^{2s}>0$, symmetric truncations to $|k|_\infty\le M$ converge in the weighted $\ell^2$ norm by convergence of the defining nonnegative series. The conjugate-symmetry condition is preserved by these cutoffs, so the completion is exactly the real weighted coefficient subspace. For $s\ge0$, $w_k^{2s}\ge1$, hence the coefficient sequence is in $\ell^2$ and [F4] gives its unique initially complex $L^2$ class. For each component $f$ of this class, complex conjugation preserves $L^2$ and the normalized coefficient convention gives
$$\widehat{\overline f}(k)=\overline{\widehat f(-k)}=\overline{a_{-k}}=a_k=\widehat f(k),$$
where $a_k$ is its coefficient coordinate. Uniqueness of Fourier synthesis in [F4] therefore gives $f=\overline f$ almost everywhere, so $\operatorname{Re}f$ is a real representative with the same coefficients. Applying this to the finitely many components gives a real $\mathbb R^N$-valued representative, unique up to equality almost everywhere by the coefficient isometry in step 2.1. For $s<0$ the construction gives only the weighted coefficient completion and makes no $L^2$ claim.
